title: Helping shape the future of the UK space sector
text:
Billions of pounds are set to be invested in the UK’s space sector under the government’s new UK Space Strategy . It aims to drive economic growth, strengthen national security and support technologies that underpin modern life.

The Government Actuary’s Department (GAD) supported the UK Space Agency (UKSA) through actuarial analysis and risk assessment to help inform a package of regulatory reforms accompanying the strategy.

title: Thousands of young disabled people to be offered guaranteed jobs
text:
Young people set to benefit from fully funded jobs as government continues to tackle UK’s persistently high disability employment gap.

Number of NEET young people who report having a disability has doubled in the past decade.

New fast track for those on health benefits part of £2.5 billion investment to support almost a million young people towards employment.

title: Recruitment for a Pharmaceutical Quality Assessor
text:
We have a vacancy for a Pharmaceutical Quality Assessor.

Pharmaceutical Quality Assessor

SSO

£47,557 per annum with Pension Scheme

Commencing at 25 days

The main role of the Quality team is to assess quality data submitted by companies in support of applications for marketing authorisations for veterinary medicines, and applications to vary these authorisations.

title: UK steps up support for global efforts to prepare for El Niño following devastating extreme weather
text:
UK funding will support hundreds of thousands around the world to prepare for droughts, floods and food shortages before they escalate into humanitarian emergencies.

Announcement follows devastating extreme weather this year, and will mitigate global impact by helping vulnerable communities protect livestock, reinforce homes and provide support to farmers before disaster hits.

title: National Armaments Director appoints new Chief Financial Officer
text:
Ian brings more than 40 years of finance leadership experience spanning professional services, global pharmaceuticals and luxury retail to the NAD Group.

As CFO, Ian will join the NAD Group Executive Committee and play a crucial role in how the NAD Group delivers the Defence Investment Plan (DIP), reacting to Defence’s new capability priorities. Under his leadership, the Group’s finance professionals will support the NAD Group teams responsible for developing, delivering, sustaining, housing and harbouring the UK’s ‘national arsenal’ and defence estate.

title: Government’s digital employment tools help thousands take the next step into work
text:
Around 20,000 people have used DWP ’s Work Hub CV builder since launch in June

Thousands receiving personalised job support through platform’s AI -powered Work Assistant

Part of Government action to harness technology, expand opportunity and boost growth in every postcode

Tens of thousands of jobseekers have already benefited from the Government’s new digital employment support tools, helping people build CVs, prepare for interviews and take the next step into work.

title: UK backing unlocks £167 million of exports for British businesses in Angola
text:
UK Export Finance (UKEF), the UK’s export credit agency, is providing £655 million in financing to support the design, construction and refurbishment of four major infrastructure projects across Angola, unlocking £167 million in supply contracts for UK businesses.

The projects, which include the design and construction of Cabinda Airport alongside significant road and other infrastructure developments, will create opportunities for British contractors and suppliers across the UK. The support will strengthen economic ties between the UK and Angola while helping to secure jobs and economic growth in communities across Britain.

title: Great North Road Solar and Biodiversity Park development consent decision announced
text:
The application is for a Solar photovoltaic array generating station, battery energy storage system and grid connection infrastructure, with a maximum generation capacity of 800MW.

The application was submitted to the Planning Inspectorate for consideration by Elements Green Trent Limited on 27 June 2025 and accepted for examination on 22 July 2025.

title: Government backs recommendations of NHS doctors-led AI Commission
text:
The government has today, 6 October 2026, confirmed it will accept all 44 recommendations made by the National Commission into the Regulation of AI in Healthcare, published 10 September, and has set out how they will be delivered across the UK. Alongside the response, the MHRA is opening the call for applications for the third phase of AI Airlock, its regulatory sandbox for AI-enabled medical devices, with testing themes directly informed by the Commission’s recommendations.

The Commission concluded that the current regulatory approach must evolve for AI technologies by designing a more proportionate, lifecycle-based framework.

title: Nearly 50 arrests in people smuggling crackdown at Irish border
text:
Immigration Enforcement has handed a blow to organised criminal gangs illegally smuggling people from Ireland to the UK, with 49 arrests across 3 days of targeted action at UK ports.

Between Tuesday 22 September and Thursday 24 September, law enforcement agencies patrolled a number of seaports, airports, roads and rail networks across Northern Ireland, Scotland, England and Wales in a bid to catch those circumventing UK immigration laws.

title: Chief Constable joins Ceremony of Remembrance
text:
Chief Constable Simon Chesterman joined senior police officers and colleagues at the UK Police Memorial to pay his respects to fallen police officers and staff at a Ceremony of Remembrance to honour the courage, service and sacrifice of police officers and staff who have given their lives in the service of others.

Two officers of the Civil Nuclear Constabulary are recorded in the Role of Honour, PC Daryl Street who died in 2021 following a road traffic collision while travelling home from duty, and PC Marcus Bennett, who died on duty in 2025 from a sudden medical episode.

title: Trawsfynydd takes next step towards Reactor Height Reduction
text:
The handover follows the award of a key contract to Costain in October 2025 to deliver reactor height reduction at Trawsfynydd.

One of the most significant programmes currently underway across the NRS estate, the project will reduce the height of both reactor buildings by nearly half. It will transform the site’s skyline, deliver the most visible change seen at Trawsfynydd in decades, and generate valuable learning that can be applied to future decommissioning projects across the UK.

title: First phase of new homes delivered for military families in Cyprus
text:
The first of 138 new homes for armed forces personnel and their families have been completed and handed over at Dhekelia Station in Cyprus.

The first phase of the project is now complete, with the delivery of 46 new Service Family Accommodation (SFA) properties in the Eastern Sovereign Base Area.

The homes have been delivered through the APOLLO programme, a joint initiative between the Defence Infrastructure Organisation (DIO) and Cyber and Specialist Operations Command (CSOC). The programme aims to enhance the resilience of critical UK defence assets in Cyprus while ensuring infrastructure meets modern building standards and supports contemporary ways of working.

title: Sir John Kingman appointed as Great British Railways Chair
text:
appointment marks next stage in journey to bring railways back under public control

His exceptional record across government and industry makes him precisely the leader we need to steer Great British Railways through this landmark transformation.

I look forward to working with him as we deliver a more reliable railway that this country can be proud of.

title: UKHSA expands wastewater surveillance to strengthen ‘early warning system’ for dangerous pathogens
text:
The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has announced today that their wastewater and environmental surveillance programme is expanding to strengthen the UK’s ability to detect pathogens with significant public health threat.

The new programme, called PRISM (Pathogen Risk Intelligence through Surveillance and Modelling), builds on the development programme for wastewater monitoring launched by UKHSA in April 2025. The development programme tested new technologies that are able to detect dangerous viruses in wastewater. It generated valuable data and insights, demonstrating the potential of environmental surveillance to strengthen the UK’s ability to detect and monitor emerging health threats. Building on these advances, PRISM is expanding into an England-wide system, strengthening existing surveillance and the country’s ability to detect outbreaks.

title: County lines –  record year for gang busts and knife seizures
text:
Record numbers of drug dealing lines have been shut down, dangerous criminals brought to justice and knives taken off Britain’s streets under the government’s relentless crackdown on county lines gangs.

New figures show last year was the best year on record for the Home Office’s County Lines Programme, set up to tackle the ruthless drug dealing gangs who use children and vulnerable people to run drugs from city centres to small towns.

title: Son of soldier killed in Iraq opens new building named for his father
text:
The block was named the Muir Building in honour of SSgt Chris Muir, an Ammunition Technician who was killed serving Iraq in 2003. His son Ben Muir was invited to cut the ribbon and officially open the block, watched by SSgt Muir’s extended family and a number of former colleagues.

SSgt Muir was based at DM Kineton as an instructor prior to his deployment to Iraq and was sadly killed during an explosive ordnance disposal operation. Naming the block after him serves as a lasting reminder to future generations of Ammunition Technicians of the courage, professionalism and unwavering commitment to duty that he embodied throughout his career.

title: Food Standards Agency and Food Standards Scotland publish latest package of guidance to support innovative food businesses
text:
The guidance covers regulatory authorisation and the assessment of growth media components and toxicology . Together, they give innovative food businesses clearer, more detailed advice on how existing food regulations apply to cell-cultivated products, helping them prepare stronger applications and understand the standards they must meet to bring products safely to market in Great Britain.

Each batch of guidance we publish makes the path to market authorisation clearer and more predictable for companies developing cell-cultivated products, while ensuring consumer safety remains at the core of everything we do. Through the Sandbox programme, we’re building a shared understanding of how food regulations apply to genuinely novel products, and turning that understanding into practical guidance the whole sector can benefit from.

title: UKDI relaunches Security Open Call
text:
UK Defence Innovation (UKDI) has relaunched the Security Open Call, which seeks disruptive technologies that can help address some of the UK’s most pressing security challenges.

This cycle of the Security Open Call focuses on Home Office and National Protective Security Authority (NPSA) priorities including cyber resilience, border security and protective security technologies.

title: Investment in Rollestone Camp supports welfare of training troops
text:
The new kitchen at Rollestone Camp on Salisbury Plain, which will feed up to 600 personnel across two sittings, is improving facilities for hundreds of Armed Forces personnel and supporting the Army to operate more sustainably.

The new facility is part of a significant programme of investment which will see new or upgraded kitchen and dining facilities at a number of training camps across the country to improve the experience of the Armed Forces.

title: Full steam ahead: new station for Bradford
text:
new station at Bradford Interchange to bring passengers more reliable services, better connections and faster journeys as Northern Powerhouse Rail moves one step closer

new station will transform the city’s connections with some of the North’s largest cities, including Leeds, Manchester and York

Passengers across Yorkshire are set to benefit from major station improvements, as the government has today (20 October 2026) confirmed a new station at Bradford Interchange.

title: Graves of five soldiers killed in Normandy identified
text:
The graves of five soldiers who went missing during the Battle of Normandy have been identified and were rededicated this week. A commemorative service honouring all five men, was also held at the British Normandy Memorial in Ver-sur-Mer (30 September 26).

Rededication services took place at CWGC St Charles-de-Percy War Cemetery for Private ( Pte ) George Chapman of 1st Battalion The Herefordshire Regiment (29 September 26), at CWGC Bayeux War Cemetery for Private Vincent Coia of 7th Battalion The Seaforth Highlanders and Lance Corporal ( LCpl ) Reginald Cyril Dewey of 4th Battalion The Lincolnshire Regiment (30 September 26), at CWGC Hottot-les-Bagues War Cemetery for Serjeant ( Sjt ) Frederick Albert Harrison of 1st Battalion The Dorsetshire Regiment and at CWGC Ranville War Cemetery for Corporal ( Cpl ) Henry Thomas Read of 8th Battalion The Rifle Brigade (1 October 26).

title: UK engineering firm appointed to deliver major decommissioning project at Dungeness A
text:
Worth up to £190 million, the contract will help accelerate the safe decommissioning of the site, reduce long-term national risk and support British industry, skills and economic opportunities for local communities.

The project will remove eight boiler units, each weighing around 800 tonnes, together with associated plant and infrastructure. It follows four years of enabling work to prepare the site for this complex phase of delivery.

title: CMA secures compensation for heating oil customers
text:
Thousands of pounds in compensation expected after customers were forced to buy replacement heating oil following price spikes

Customers who did not buy replacement heating oil will have their original orders honoured

Suppliers under review have now agreed to pay compensation under the CMA’s scheme

Affected customers will be contacted directly and do not need to take any action at this stage

title: PM meeting with President of the European Commission Ursula von der Leyen: 22 September 2026
text:
The two leaders discussed the importance of working towards a successful outcome for the next EU-UK summit later in the year.

They also reflected on the challenges the EU and UK face in responding to the threats from Russia in Ukraine and in relation to hybrid warfare and disinformation.

They emphasised the importance of working together to meet the common security threats faced by Europe, to reduce illegal migration and to respond to unfair competition and overcapacity in global markets.

title: Bass boost for hook and line fishers
text:
Owners and masters of single hull under-8 metre vessels will be picked through a written application followed by a randomised ballot for those who show they are eligible under the terms of the process.

The authorisations are currently not being used and will enable successful applicants to fish with hook and line only. They will be limited to vessels that do not currently have a bass authorisation.

title: Stronger safeguards for wheelchair users and better-trained staff to support disabled air passengers
text:
greater protection for disabled passengers, with action to prevent wheelchairs being damaged

airline and airport staff to receive better training designed to help disabled passengers get the assistance they need

improvements come as Civil Aviation Bill progresses through Parliament, and will help create greater protections for disabled passengers

Disabled passengers will be better protected from having wheelchairs damaged when they fly and will receive better support from trained airport and airline staff, as new accessibility improvements are rolled out across the aviation industry.

title: Edition 44: News from the Adjudicator
text:
My annual conference is taking place on Tuesday 29 September.

The conference will bring together suppliers, retailers and industry representatives. It will reflect on the GCA’s work to ensure fair treatment of suppliers and on the support available to suppliers, including how they can raise issues in confidence. YouGov will also present a detailed analysis of the 2026 annual survey results.

title: From bomb‑proof pants to laser weapons: 25 years of Dstl
text:
Established in 2001 following the part‑privatisation of the Defence Evaluation and Research Agency ( DERA ), the Defence Science and Technology Laboratory ( Dstl ) is the Ministry of Defence’s in-government science and technology organisation, providing unique expertise, crucial insights and innovative mission-winning solutions essential for maintaining UK warfighting readiness in an increasingly dangerous and complex world.

Dstl sustains critical sovereign capabilities including chemical and biological defence and explosives forensics, as well as specialising in more than 20 science and technology areas such as AI , quantum, directed energy weapons, cyber, robotics and autonomous systems both for defence and national security.

title: Back Zelenskyy and Ukraine with an energy ceasefire, Foreign Secretary tells European partners
text:
He will call for an end to attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure, and underline UK’s determination to act together with its European partners including to defend against Russian hybrid attacks across the continent

UK will stress that no ally is immune from Russia’s tactics, and that now is the time to double down on protecting UK security by building a stronger Europe in a stronger NATO

title: New tools to support preparation for Martyn's Law
text:
The Security Industry Authority (SIA) is releasing new planning tools today to support premises and events in scope of Martyn’s Law as they prepare to comply with the new legislation. Martyn’s Law, which is expected to come into force in spring 2027, aims to keep people safe by ensuring that publicly accessible premises and events are better prepared against acts of terrorism.

The SIA is urging all those in scope to use the new planning tools to start to prepare for the incoming legislation.

title: Government's Jobs Guarantee turns promise into paycheques for young people
text:
Scheme aims to create opportunity for those furthest from the jobs market and is backed by major businesses, including Boots and OCS

Over 90,000 fully funded jobs to be created by 2029 through the Jobs Guarantee, a key part of the Government’s £2.5 billion drive to tackle youth unemployment

The Jobs Guarantee scheme offers a direct route into work for all 18–24-year-olds who have been claiming Universal Credit and looking for work for 18 months.

title: Animal use in veterinary vaccines quality control falls to lowest levels in a decade
text:
Far fewer animals are being used to release batches of veterinary vaccines than a decade ago, new figures published today (Thursday 24 September) by the Veterinary Medicines Directorate (VMD) show.

The average number of animals needed to check the quality, safety and effectiveness of a single batch of animal vaccine fell by 41% - from 29 animals in 2013 to 17 in 2024.

title: UK recognises positive development through European Long Range Strike Approach
text:
Two years ago, the Defence Ministers of France, Germany, Italy, Poland, Sweden and the United Kingdom decided to launch the European Long-range Strike Approach.

By launching this approach, the Ministers recognized that the ability to conduct conventional long-range strikes had become a critical capability in contemporary warfare that is crucial to have at disposal. Our common ambition was to pave the way for short to long-term cooperation for the European defence industrial and technological base to develop, produce and deliver the appropriate equipment, in appropriate numbers, within an appropriate schedule.

title: £21.8m funding boost to help councils build more affordable homes
text:
More councils will be able to bring forward ambitious affordable housing plans thanks to a £21.8 million boost to the Council Housebuilding Support Fund ( CHSF ).

Available until March 2029, the revenue funding will help local authorities build the skills, capacity and partnerships needed to develop strong bids for the Social and Affordable Homes Programme ( SAHP ).

title: Eight Welsh organisations strike Gold
text:
The eight employers from across Wales were recognised for the outstanding support they give to the Armed Forces community at the awards ceremony held at HMS Cambria, Cardiff Bay, on 24 September.

The glittering awards evening began with a drinks reception with guests treated to music from Cerys Rees, regimental harpist of The Royal Welsh. Guests were also entertained by The Band of His Majesty’s Royal Marines Plymouth Brass Quintet.

title: 150 rural 4G masts now live so holidaymakers can switch off without being cut off
text:
More than 150 government-funded 4G mast upgrades are now live across the UK through the Shared Rural Network, bringing 4G coverage from EE, Virgin Media O2, and Vodafone and ThreeUK to some of Britain’s hardest-to-reach rural areas.

Britain’s walkers, hikers and holidaymakers can stay connected, check weather and route information, and contact emergency services more easily when needed.

title: £16m legal lifeline for families facing eviction and hardship
text:
Legal lifelines grant to help people struggling with debt and housing crises

Early support to help stop legal disputes spiralling into poverty and court

Part of Government’s plan to give British families greater breathing space

Launching tomorrow (01 October), the Government has announced a multi-million-pound Legal Support Grant, to enable those in need to access trusted advice and practical support when facing some of life’s toughest challenges.

title: PM statement on October 7th attacks
text:
Three years on from the October 7 attacks on Israel, we remember those who were senselessly killed by Hamas terrorists.

The impact of the attacks has been felt not just in Israel, but in Jewish communities across the world who still bear the burden of the tragic events that day.

In the years since, we have seen a disturbing rise in antisemitic behaviour in the UK.

title: Celebrity parents back government campaign
text:
A new survey reveals 82% of parents want their family to be more active together, but 6 in 10 (61%) don’t think they’re ‘good enough’ at sport

EastEnders actress and mum Charlie Brooks has joined the nation’s fitness coach and dad Joe Wicks to launch the ‘New Moves Club’ encouraging families across the country to try a new activity together in a bid to get more families active

title: Helping communities stay ahead of flooding along the Great Ouse
text:
This is where prolonged dry conditions can be followed by periods of heavy rainfall and flooding.

With severe drought recently declared in parts of southern England, and a heightened potential for a wet winter, communities can face contrasting challenges of water scarcity and flooding, sometimes in the same season. The Environment Agency is encouraging communities to prepare for the risks ahead as part of its Flood Action Week campaign.

title: Professor David Strain appointed as DWP Chief Medical Advisor
text:
He joins DWP from the University of Exeter, the NHS and the Parliamentary Office of Science and Technology ( POST ), where he has served as Thematic Research Lead for Health.

I am delighted to be joining DWP as Chief Medical Advisor.

Throughout my career I have been passionate about turning evidence into practical improvements for people, particularly those living with long-term health conditions.

title: No one should have to fight for time to grieve” - New rights for family bereavement and pregnancy loss
text:
People who have lost loved ones to have legal right to take time off work as new rights to also include step, half, adoptive, kinship care and foster relationships

Women and their partners who have had any type of pregnancy loss will be entitled to two week’s leave

Latest development in the plan to Make Work Pay to help people to stay in work, improve living standards and ease pressures on family life.

title: Trials across the country accelerated for fast and fair justice
text:
Domestic abuse, drug and knife crime cases to be prioritised by certain courts

Part of nationwide drive to cut the court backlog and get fast, fair justice for victims

Expansion comes as the Courts and Tribunals Bill returns to Parliament

Judges, supported by court staff, are using the initiative – previously known as Blitz Courts – to help cut mounting court delays that have left victims waiting years for justice.

title: Chancellor announces Bank of England appointments
text:
David Craig and Paul Nowak are appointed to four-year terms until 31 August 2030. Hanneke Smits will begin her four-year term on 1 January 2027, until 31 December 2030.

These appointments strengthen the Court at a critical moment for the UK economy, providing deep and varied experience to support the Bank in delivering its core missions of monetary and financial stability.

title: Households living near new pylons to save thousands on bills
text:
Government reveals the communities in over 40 locations eligible for cheaper electricity bills

Households near new pylons could save up to £2,500 over 10 years

Upgrading an electricity grid largely built in the 1960s will lower energy costs for households across Britain

Thousands of households living near new or upgraded pylons are set to get money off their electricity bills. Payments will start from next year, as the first projects expected to be in scope of the government’s bill discount scheme are unveiled today (Wednesday 12 August).

title: Information Commission succeeds the ICO as UK's data protection regulator
text:
The new Commission will continue to oversee how organisations use and protect people’s personal data, helping to ensure it is handled responsibly.

People should have confidence that their personal information is being used responsibly, whether they are accessing public services, shopping online or using new digital technologies.

The new Information Commission will continue to provide strong, independent oversight of data protection, while bringing together a range of expertise to ensure the regulator remains equipped to respond to future challenges and opportunities in a fast-changing digital world.

title: PM vows to save “hollowed out high streets” with crackdown on vape and betting shops
text:
Dodgy businesses linked to organised crime to be shut down for longer under tougher powers for police and local authorities

The measures will put communities back in control of their high streets by giving local people a real say over what businesses can open in their town centres and how local high streets should look, as well as tougher powers for the police and local authorities to crack down on rogue operators.

title: Recruitment campaign inspired by officers' experiences launches
text:
Developed with serving officers, the campaign puts their experiences at its heart, highlighting the many roles, responsibilities and perspectives that shape who they are both within and beyond policing.

Using officers’ own words and stories, the campaign demonstrates that policing is only one part of their identity, showcasing the experiences and circumstances that have shaped their lives and careers. It aims to give potential applicants a genuine insight into life at the Civil Nuclear Constabulary ( CNC ) and challenge assumptions about who can succeed in policing.

title: Foreign Secretary statement on the UK's diplomatic presence in Jerusalem
text:
We have been clear that we do not accept that the Government of Israel has the legal right to close the British Consulate General in Jerusalem, which has been there for nearly 200 years. The UK government reiterates its long-standing view that East Jerusalem is occupied territory.

Following discussions with the Government of Israel, our Consulate General building will not be closing, and will be known as the UK Mission, Jerusalem from today. The UK Mission, Jerusalem is independent, operational, and will continue to deliver vital services and our work with the Palestinian people.

title: Your cancellation’s covered: new scheme to help stranded rail passengers arrives this weekend
text:
for the first time, passengers whose trains are cancelled can use another operator’s service to complete their journey immediately, free of charge

ends passenger limbo and last-minute bills for replacement tickets

latest move to put public service back at the heart of the railway ahead of the creation of Great British Railways

From Sunday (20 September 2026), passengers whose trains are cancelled will be able to use other services free of charge – ending limbo at stations and the need for costly re-bookings.

title: First regional solar breakdown as installations hit record highs
text:
Across the UK, nearly 172,000 solar installations have been fitted since the start of 2026, with increases across every UK nation and English region over the last 12 months

Rooftop solar is helping to drive the surge - accounting for more than 7 in 10 installations during July

Comes as retailers including Currys, B&Q, Screwfix and Amazon prepare to roll out plug-in solar, following work with government

title: UKHSA updates heat health alerts across England
text:
The UK Health Security Agency ( UKHSA ) has extended the current amber heat-health alert ( HHA ) for the East Midlands, West Midlands, South East, South West, London and East of England until 10am on Saturday 15 August. All other regions in England remain under an amber alert until 9pm today, Friday 14 August.

The UK Health Security Agency ( UKHSA ) has escalated the heat-health alert ( HHA ) for the North East from yellow to amber, effective from 9am on Tuesday 11 August until 9pm on Friday 14 August. The existing amber alerts in other regions remain unchanged.

title: Pat Ritchie’s tenure as Homes England Chair extended
text:
This comes at a significant time for Homes England as we continue to evolve to support the government’s priorities and help realise the ambitions of places and communities across the country.

I am personally very proud to continue working with such a dedicated and capable team. The coming months will bring both change and opportunity as we work alongside government, mayors and local leaders to deliver their ambitions, helping to create thriving places and deliver lasting impact for people and communities.

title: Government publishes reports on improving building safety
text:
Interim Chief Construction Adviser publishes final report, reflecting on the building safety system

Comes as the government publishes the latest quarterly Grenfell Tower Inquiry progress report

Nine further recommendations completed, including improving national training and guidance for fire and rescue services

New reports published today set out the final reflections from the Interim Chief Construction Adviser, as well as the government’s latest progress against the recommendations made in the Grenfell Tower Inquiry Phase 2 report.

title: Independent Commission led by NHS doctors sets out blueprint to accelerate safe AI adoption in healthcare
text:
The National Commission into the Regulation of AI in Healthcare has today, 10 September 2026, published its recommendations on how the UK can strengthen the regulation of AI in healthcare, so it remains safe, keeps pace with innovation, and continues to earn people’s trust.

AI is already used in the NHS to spot serious health problems early, for example strokes and skin cancers, and to free up clinicians’ time through voice-enabled technologies. The Commission’s recommendations aim to help many more patients benefit safely and quickly, by supporting the UK to become the best place for innovators to build and safely test AI, the best place for healthcare professionals to use it and, most importantly, the best place for patients to engage with it in their care.

title: New Belfast fabrication hall to support shipbuilding for decades
text:
New fabrication hall opens today at Navantia UK’s Harland & Wolff site in Belfast, the centrepiece of a £157 million investment programme across their four UK shipyards.

The hall will support construction of three new Fleet Solid Support ships for the Royal Fleet Auxiliary, and 900 skilled jobs and apprenticeships in Belfast.

Follows record-breaking defence investment in Northern Ireland’s industry, which rose by 63% in real terms in 2025/26 to £464 million.

title: British exporters to be given greater access to finance as UKEF strengthens support for Ukraine
text:
Changes will widen access to the scheme, helping more businesses – particularly smaller firms – beginning their exporting journey to secure the working capital they need to grow overseas

UKEF’s financial capacity for Ukraine to rise by £3 billion to £6.5 billion, enabling further support for priority projects and British exports

Smaller businesses will find it easier to access millions of pounds of government-backed finance to grow their exports under an expansion of UK Export Finance (UKEF) support announced in the Budget.

title: Upfront help cuts placement costs for healthcare students
text:
Upfront cash help for nursing, midwifery, allied health, and dental therapy and hygiene students’ placement costs, meeting commitment set out in the 10 Year Health Plan

Students spared from paying excess placement travel and accommodation bills out of their own pockets as government works to help with cost of living

Boost for rural and coastal placements where costs can be highest

title: Recruitment for two Veterinary Pharmacovigilance Inspectors
text:
We have two vacancies for Veterinary Pharmacovigilance Inspectors.

Veterinary Pharmacovigilance Inspector

G7

£64,015 per annum with Pension Scheme

Commencing at 25 days

The Pharmacovigilance Inspector ensures that Marketing Authorisation Holders (MAHs) comply with their legal obligations for pharmacovigilance in accordance with Veterinary Medicines Regulations 2013 (as amended) (VMR) and EU 2019/6.

title: Victims of abuse to be better supported by their community
text:
Government launches campaign to help everyone know how to Respond to disclosures of abuse

Crucial step on Government’s mission to halve violence against women and girls within a decade

The first moment when someone opens up about abuse is crucial and the response they get may determine what happens next - whether they go on to seek further help, report their experiences to police and begin to recover, or whether they feel dismissed, judged and never speak about it again.

title: Invitation to an IIAC meeting on 22 October 2026
text:
The aim of the meeting is to give members of the public, their representatives, and people with a professional interest in occupational diseases, the opportunity to learn about and ask questions regarding the council’s work.

The meeting will take place on Thursday 22 October 2026 from 2pm to 5pm at:

The Midland Hotel 16 Peter Street Manchester M60 2DS

title: Gwyndod supply chain mobilised to deliver UK’s first SMRs
text:
More than 400 suppliers from across North Wales, the UK and the international nuclear industry came together on Ynys Môn as Rolls-Royce SMR and Great British Energy – Nuclear (GBE-N) moved forward with plans to deliver the UK’s first small modular reactors at Gwyndod.

The ‘Delivering Together’ conference, held at Coleg Menai’s Llangefni Campus, brought businesses face-to-face with the joint Gwyndod delivery team. It marked an important step in mobilising the supply chain and building the industrial capability needed to deliver this flagship project.

title: Your new go-to guide for every stage of your IAA journey
text:
The IAA has published a new guidance document to help both current and aspiring advisers more easily access the information they need on registration, regulation and professional standards.

The new document responds to feedback that it has not always been easy to find the right information at the right time. By setting out key processes, requirements and regulatory expectations in one place, the IAA aims to make guidance simpler to use and easier to navigate.

title: More enriching activities for hundreds of thousands of children
text:
Hundreds of thousands more young people in disadvantaged communities will get the chance to join sports teams, learn an instrument, or take part in debating and outdoor adventures, helping them build confidence, develop new skills and stay engaged both in and out of education.

More than 400 secondary schools will benefit from tailored support backed by £22.5 million through the government’s Enrichment Expansion programme.

title: MHRA approves new oral treatment for moderate to severe plaque psoriasis
text:
The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) has approved icotrokinra hydrochloride (Icotyde) for the treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults and adolescents aged 12 years and older who weigh at least 40 kg and are candidates for systemic therapy.

Plaque psoriasis is an inflammatory condition that causes red, scaly and often itchy or painful patches of skin. It can affect areas including the scalp, genitals, hands and feet, as well as the nails.

title: Time to end class squeamishness: first government unit to improve life chances for working class
text:
A new class unit will drive forward government work to improve life chances

Social Mobility Commission to be closed down as part of wider government review into arm’s length bodies

New unit to focus on improving lives of low-income families, disadvantaged communities and rooting out child poverty

The new unit will bring social mobility work into the heart of government, with the Social Mobility Commission (SMC) closing as part of the government’s wider review of arm’s length bodies to ensure work is delivered as effectively as possible.

title: Anniversary Statement: Cessna 210L, N1110S
text:
This statement provides an update on the ongoing AAIB investigation into an accident involving a Cessna 210L, N1110S, at Providenciales International Airport, Turks and Caicos Islands, on 29 July 2025.

On final approach to the airport, the aircraft’s engine ran roughly and subsequently lost power. The aircraft struck the ground in the undershoot to the runway fatally injuring the pilot and seriously injuring the passenger.

title: Joint Statement on Iran, 12 October
text:
The Foreign Ministers of Albania, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Canada, Croatia, Czech Republic, Cyprus, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, New Zealand, North Macedonia, Norway, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, the United Kingdom and the United States, and the High Representative of the European Union condemn in the strongest terms Iran’s use of violent attacks, including the acts of lethal plotting, arson, sabotage, cyber-attacks, and other hybrid activities against us and our partners.

We recognise the United Kingdom’s attribution of Iran’s involvement in the incident at RAF Fairford on 27 September. The UK has also concluded this event demonstrates the IRGC’s continued willingness to project hostile activity beyond its borders through covert networks and proxy actors.

title: Minister intervenes to keep iconic bust of Edward the Black Prince in the UK
text:
The export bar allows time for a UK gallery or institution to acquire this national treasure

The government has placed a temporary export ban on the sculpture in the hope of keeping it accessible to the UK public. The deferral period gives time for museums and galleries to raise the funds needed to acquire the bust, for example through philanthropic support, or for a private individual to purchase it and donate it to the nation.

title: Progress made in cleaning up Companies House register as further steps taken to tackle economic crime
text:
The report is the latest update into the implementation of parts 1 to 3 of the Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023 (ECCT Act) which brought about the most significant reforms to UK company law in almost 2 centuries.

From credit to purchasing, the register plays a key role in informing a vast number of business decisions every day. A more accurate and robust register will inform better decision-making, bolstering confidence and supporting growth of the UK economy.

title: Update to Bona Vacantia Land and Buildings guidelines
text:
The Bona Vacantia Division has today published revised Refer Bona Vacantia Land or Buildings (BVC2) and Apply to buy a Freehold Reversion (BVC4) guidelines.

This is to incorporate increases in the indicative charges relating to the District Valuer fees where there is a requirement for a valuation to be obtained in relation to the Land/Buildings or Freehold/Leasehold Reversion.

title: You've got the grades, but don't pass on your health
text:
The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) congratulates everyone celebrating their A level results today (13 August). With the prospect of heading to university a few short weeks away, now is the time for young people to check they are up to date with their vaccinations and have the medicines and medical devices they need to stay well as they hit freshers’ week. These tips will stand you in good stead even if you’re taking another route following your results.

Meningitis B is a serious infection which can have long-term impact on your health and is potentially life-threatening. It can be contagious, so students living in university halls or shared accommodation and socialising together can be particularly at risk.

title: Bloomsbury Institute's student sponsor licence revoked
text:
The Bloomsbury Institute, a higher education provider in central London, has had its licence to sponsor international students revoked after failing to meet the Basic Compliance Assessment.

The Basic Compliance Assessment is an annual check that all sponsors must pass, measuring visa refusal rates, course enrolment and completion.

At the time of the assessment, sponsors were required to meet three thresholds: a visa refusal rate of less than 10%, an enrolment rate of at least 90%, and a course completion rate of at least 85%.

title: Mayors and local leaders work with No10 North to drive search for 'top 10' biggest strategic investment sites across country
text:
Mayors and local leaders will help identify opportunities as government works to unlock up to 10 major industrial and commercial sites across the UK.

The Strategic Sites Accelerator will deploy around £700 million, alongside expert support to tackle barriers including planning, grid connections and access to finance.

Programme aims to crowd in up to £2 billion in private investment and could support tens of thousands of jobs over time.

title: PM call with the Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia: 27 July 2026
text:
The two leaders discussed the crisis in Gaza, where they both outlined the importance of a two-state solution between Palestine and Israel.

The leaders also looked ahead to next year which will mark 100 years since the signing of the Treaty of Jeddah, recognising its importance in the relationship between the two nations.

The leaders looked forward to speaking again soon.

title: Two men arrested after illegal waste dumping in Cheshire
text:
The Environment Agency contacted Cheshire Police on Friday morning, 7 August, for assistance with an arrest as part of an investigation into a large-scale illegal waste site at a farm on Coal Pit Lane near Middlewich.

Both organisations attended the site as part of ongoing enforcement activity.

A 69-year-old local man was arrested at the site on suspicion of waste offences. He has since been released on bail while investigations continue.
